atoms.b: The word amphibian has a Greek origin and can be translated as “double life”. This word is very fitting because amphibians spend the first part of their lives in water and the second part on ((++land ships)).
The life cycle of amphibians is very special because they go through many ((++physical educational)) changes while growing into adulthood. This process is called ((++metamorphosis surgery)).

Salamanders, just like frogs, toads and newts are ((mammals ++amphibians)). All these animals experience metamorphosis while growing up. Let’s have a closer look at the different stages of a salamander’s life cycle.

text: This picture shows the salamander’s life cycle.
hint.label: Salamander’s Life Cycle

a.sound: Stage one begins with the laying of the eggs.
In stage two the salamander is called a larva. At this point, larvae live in water and don’t have limbs yet.
In the third stage, the larva starts to develop limbs and lungs. This transformation is important for its future on land.
The fourth stage is the final stage in the salamander’s life cycle. At this point, the salamander has climbed out of the water and will live the rest of its life on land.
